identity.title: Representation Alignment for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers Is Easier Than You Think

problem.claim: Large-scale diffusion generation may bottleneck on effectively learning useful visual representations.

gap.claim: Diffusion-induced representations are meaningful but lag behind those learned by recent self-supervised methods.

contributions.claim: Introduces REPA, a regularizer aligning projections of noisy hidden states with clean-image representations from pretrained visual encoders.
Reports improved training efficiency and generation quality for diffusion and flow-based transformers, including DiTs and SiTs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present external-representation alignment as a straightforward way to make diffusion-transformer training easier.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report over 17.5× faster SiT training, reaching the performance of a 7M-step SiT-XL trained in under 400K steps, without classifier-free guidance.
The authors report FID=1.42 with classifier-free guidance using the guidance interval.
The authors report significant efficiency and generation-quality gains across popular diffusion and flow-based transformers.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion denoising can produce meaningful representations, but they trail recent self-supervised representations.
The authors identify representation learning as a main bottleneck for large-scale diffusion generation.
They propose using high-quality external visual representations through the REPA alignment regularizer.
Applied to DiTs and SiTs, REPA is reported to improve efficiency and generation quality, including a 17.5× SiT speedup and FID 1.42.

source_observation.claim: The paper connects a training bottleneck to a specific representational mismatch and regularizes noisy hidden states toward clean pretrained features.

lessons.interpretation: A concrete bottleneck-to-alignment framing can make a proposed training intervention easier to motivate and evaluate.
lessons.application: For another generative model, identify an internal representation gap, define an explicit target from a suitable pretrained encoder, and state which hidden states are aligned.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when external representations are unavailable, mismatched to the target domain, or impose unacceptable computational or dependency costs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, statistical variation, or the exact evaluation protocol for the reported gains.
The benchmark context and guidance-interval details for FID=1.42 are not provided.
It is unclear whether the reported SiT comparison controls all architecture, data, and compute differences.
